quick_read.weather_md: **Weather:** 28°C high / 17°C low. Mostly sunny, rain odds low. Leave the umbrella home, bro — won't need it.
quick_read.uv_md: **UV:** Sitting at 8, which is "very high." Slap on **SPF 30+ broad spectrum** before you walk out, throw a cap on. Around 2pm, splash water on your face and re-apply. Future you says thanks.
quick_read.uv_advisory_md: *📎 Goose Investigation Bureau — sourcing UV from EPA + Cancer Research UK. UV 1–2 = no protection needed. UV 3+ = sunscreen + shade + hat + sunglasses. UV 8+ = limit midday sun. UV 11+ = stay out of midday sun entirely.*
quick_read.budget_hint_md: **Daily budget — $175 average.** With my picks below, that's real. Save: bus + panino lunch knocks $40 off. Splurge: flip it for a tasting menu day. **Bonus: 2025 Jubilee is officially over (closed Jan 6, 2026), so hotels are back down from peak-pilgrim pricing. You're catching it at the good time.**
quick_read.intro_md: > *Bro, I dug into your dates, pulled the news, grabbed the spots locals actually eat at, lined up the smart moves. Below = the full goose investigation. Did my best, you're covered.*
quick_read.do_now_md:
**Do now:**
- **Book Eros Ramazzotti at Stadio Olimpico — Jun 16, right in your window.** Italian-pop legend, 70,000-strong sing-along. If you want one *very Italian* night, this is it. Tickets via TicketOne, going fast.
- **Skip Fiumicino on Jun 26.** 24h ground-crew strike, whole airport sideways. You're already gone by then, but if dates shift, replan.
- **Cash is king.** Pull **€100** day one. ATMs at Termini = fine. The "Euronet" ones near the Colosseum = €5 fee trap. Trattorias get card-shy after €20.
quick_read.restaurant_hook_md: **The Places to Eat list below is the play.** These are Michelin Guide picks — mostly *not* starred, which is the point. Excellent Roman food without the $400-per-head circus. Lock the reservations now or you'll be that guy outside in line at 8:45 staring through the window.

happening.news_md:
- **Nationwide airport strike — Jun 13.** 1pm–5pm, every Italian airport. Fiumicino + Ciampino. Outside your window, but watch if dates shift. [src 1]
- **General transit strike — Jun 19–20.** 21:00 Jun 19 → 21:00 Jun 20. Buses, metro, regional rail down. Service guaranteed only 6–9am + 6–9pm. Walk it, or pre-book a cab the day before. [src 1]
- **Jun 26 ground-crew strike — 24h, every major airport.** You return Jun 22, so you're clear. [src 2]
- **Post-Jubilee — Holy Year closed Jan 6, 2026.** Pope Leo XIV sealed the Holy Door. 33+ million pilgrims passed through in 2025; wave's over. Translation: hotels priced sane, lines at basilicas back to normal, restaurants no longer locked solid 60 days out. You're hitting Rome at the recovery moment. [src 3]
happening.sports_md: - **🎾 Padel + amateur play.** If you actually play, ASD clubs around Aventino and Trastevere take walk-ins. €15/hour court. Real local angle, not a tourist trap.
happening.entertainment_md:
- **🎤 Eros Ramazzotti — Stadio Olimpico, Jun 16.** Flagged in Do Now. Worth repeating. [src 4]
- **🎭 Rome Opera House summer festival at Circus Maximus.** Opera, cinema, dance, music under the stars at the actual ancient chariot track. Schedule rotates weekly — check `operaroma.it` for nights you're free. [src 4]
- **🎸 Rock In Roma at Circo Massimo.** Annual June series. International + Italian rock lineup. Lower-key venue than the Olimpico, easier last-minute tickets. [src 5]
- **⛪ Pope's Wednesday audience.** St. Peter's Square, 9am every Wed when Pope Leo XIV is in town. Free, ticket required via Prefecture of the Papal Household. Apply by email a week out. [src 6]

brief.watch_md:
- **Colosseum + Roman Forum combo — ~$25.** Timed-entry online, skip the 90-min line. Photo: Via Sacra looking up at the Arch of Titus at golden hour. Stupid good.
- **Trastevere at dusk — FREE.** Cobblestones, ivy, no tour buses, real Rome. Photo: Piazza Santa Maria fountain around 8:30pm when the light goes orange.
- **Foro Italico walk-through — FREE.** Italian Open Masters wrapped May 17 — Sinner won at home, first Italian since 1976. Courts closed for play but the venue is walkable. Marble statues from the 1930s Mussolini era still loom around the stadium. Off-the-tourist-track, sports-history-meets-fascist-architecture combo. [src 7]
- **Basilica of St. Paul Outside the Walls (San Paolo fuori le Mura) — FREE.** Niche pick, trust me. Every pope in history sits on the walls in medallion portraits running around the whole nave. Empty spaces left for future popes. Quietly insane. 20 min on Metro B from the center.
- **Aventine Keyhole — FREE.** Peek through a literal keyhole at the Knights of Malta, see St. Peter's framed perfectly. Five minutes.
- **Galleria Borghese — ~$15.** Bernini sculptures that look like the stone is alive. Two-hour timed slots, book 2+ weeks ahead.
brief.eat_md:
*Most are Guide-listed, not starred. Real food, not gold-card territory.*

- **Roscioli** — Bib Gourmand. The carbonara locals argue about. Reserve 3 weeks ahead, no joke. *(~$50-70 pp)*
- **Armando al Pantheon** — Guide listed. Old-school Roman, tiny room, walls covered in photos. Booking essential. *(~$45-60 pp)*
- **La Pergola** — Three stars (the exception). Only worth it for the full tasting menu. *(~$300+ pp)*
- **Pianostrada** — Guide listed. Modern Roman, garden seating. Lunch books slower than dinner. *(~$50-70 pp)*
brief.knowing_md:
- **Taxis — use FreeNow, skip Uber.** Uber crawls in Italy and drivers sometimes try to bolt on "extras." FreeNow is the local app, same UX as Uber, pulls real licensed cabs that show up in minutes. Heads-up: most drivers speak only Italian, but you tap the address in the app so it doesn't matter. Worth it.
- **Coffee — don't go to Starbucks. Anywhere is better.** Italians don't do venti-frappa-whatevers. Menu = espresso, macchiato, cappuccino (mornings only — order one after lunch and the barista clocks you instantly), Americano if you really need a mug. Every neighborhood bar makes it well. Some interiors look like a 1972 waiting room — trust it. €1.20 coffee, beats anything Starbucks ever made you.
- **Restaurant coperto.** €2–4 cover charge per person, standard, not a scam. Tip 5–10% only if service was great.
- **Pickpockets on the 64 bus.** Termini → Vatican route. Front-pocket wallet or walk part of it.
- **Water fountains are free.** The "Nasoni" run cold, clean mountain water all over the city. Refill, skip the €3 bottles.

budget_usd.notes: Mid = 3-star hotel ($110), 2 meals out ($55), gelato + 1 attraction ($25). Add $40 cabs on strike days.
